source_refs.note: Book p. 15: 1.6 definition, inverse of exponential, common/natural log, basic identities (4th misprinted), laws and change of base

blocks.text: Pichle topics mein hum ne exponential function \(y = a^{x}\) ko achhi tarah dekha: us ka graph, domain, range aur properties. Aaj hum us ka 'ulta' function seekhenge, jise logarithmic function kehte hain. Ek seedhi baat zehan mein bitha lijiye: exponential function power de kar jawab nikalta hai, aur logarithm jawab de kar power poochhta hai. Yeh topic aage poore unit (aur Calculus) mein baar baar kaam aayega, is liye isay dhyan se parhiye.

Kitab ki definition: logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) hai, jahan \(a > 0\), \(a \ne 1\) aur \(x > 0\). Yeh har positive real number \(x\) ko ek hi (unique, yani sirf ek) real number \(y\) deta hai, aisa ke \(a^{y} = x\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Logarithm sirf ek sawal ka jawab hai: base \(a\) ko kitni power di jaye ke \(x\) ban jaye? Misaal ke taur par \(\log_2 8 = 3\), kyun ke \(2^{3} = 8\). Isi tarah \(\log_3 \frac{1}{9} = -2\), kyun ke \(3^{-2} = \frac{1}{9}\). Dekhiye, logarithm ka jawab negative bhi ho sakta hai, lekin jis number ka log le rahe hain woh hamesha positive hona chahiye.
Yeh shartein (conditions) kyun lagayi gayi hain? \(a > 0\) is liye ke positive base ki har real power defined hoti hai; negative base ki power, jaise \((-2)^{1/2}\), real nahi hoti. \(a \ne 1\) is liye ke \(1\) ki har power \(1\) hi rehti hai, to base 1 se koi aur number ban hi nahi sakta. Aur \(x > 0\) is liye ke positive base ko koi bhi power do, jawab hamesha positive aata hai; is wajah se zero ya negative number ka log exist hi nahi karta.
Logarithmic Function as Inverse of Exponential Function

Ab dekhte hain ke logarithmic function exponential function ka inverse (ulta function) kyun hai. Hum jaante hain ke exponential function
\[y = a^{x},\ (a > 0,\ a \ne 1)\]
one-to-one function hai (yani do alag inputs kabhi same output nahi dete), us ka domain \(]-\infty, \infty[\) aur range \(]0, \infty[\) hai. Jo function one-to-one ho, us ka inverse ban sakta hai, yani woh invertible hai. Inverse banane ka tareeqa: \(x\) aur \(y\) ki jagah badal dein:
\[x = a^{y}\]
\[\Rightarrow y = \log_a x\]

Is tarah logarithmic function, exponential function ka inverse hai. Us ka domain \(]0, \infty[\) aur range \(]-\infty, \infty[\) hai. Ghor kijiye: exponential ka range, log ka domain ban gaya, aur exponential ka domain, log ka range ban gaya. Inverse mein yahi hota hai.

blocks.caption: Teaching note: dono functions ka muqabla (hamari taraf se, kitab mein yeh table nahi)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(x\) aur \(y\) ki adla badli hi inverse ka asal matlab hai. Ek function ke inputs doosre ke outputs hote hain. Rozmarra ki misaal: agar ek machine Celsius ko Fahrenheit mein badalti hai, to us ki inverse machine Fahrenheit ko wapas Celsius mein badalti hai; jo cheez pehli machine ka jawab thi, woh doosri ka input hai. Isi liye \(y = a^{x}\) ka har point \((p, q)\), \(y = \log_a x\) par \((q, p)\) ban jata hai. Topic 1.8 mein aap dekhenge ke yeh adla badli graph par line \(y = x\) mein reflection (aaina) ki tarah nazar aati hai.

Do bases itni zyada use hoti hain ke un ke apne naam hain. Base 10 wale logarithm ko common logarithm kehte hain, aur base \(e\) wale logarithm ko natural logarithm kehte hain. Hum likhte hain:
\[\log_{10} b = \log b\]
\[\log_e b = \ln b\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(e \approx 2.71828\) wahi khaas number hai jo aap ne topic 1.4 mein \(y = e^{x}\) ke saath dekha tha. Calculator par \(\log\) wala button common logarithm (base 10) deta hai aur \(\ln\) wala button natural logarithm (base \(e\)). Is kitab mein jab base na likha ho to \(\log\) ka matlab base 10 hai. Khud sochiye: \(\log 1000\) kitna hoga? Jawab 3, kyun ke \(10^{3} = 1000\).
Basic Logarithmic Identities
Ab chaar buniyadi identities dekhte hain. Inhein ratta lagane ki zaroorat nahi; har ek seedha definition \(a^{y} = x\) se nikalti hai. Pehle kitab ki list, phir har ek ki wajah.

Kitab kehti hai: \(a > 0\), \(a \ne 1\), \(x > 0\) ke liye yeh chaar identities (hamesha sach rehne wale rishte) hain:
\[\log_a 1 = 0\]
\[\log_a a = 1\]
\[\log_a(a^{x}) = x\]
\[a^{\log_a x} = x\]
Chautha rishta kitab mein ghalat chhapa hai; yahan sahi shakal likhi hai (neeche wala box dekhiye).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab chauthi identity \(\log_a x = x\) chhaapti hai, jo ghalat hai. Misaal: \(\log_2 8 = 3\) hai, 8 nahi. Sahi identity \(a^{\log_a x} = x\) hai (jab \(x > 0\)): base ko \(x\) ke log ki power dein to \(x\) wapas mil jata hai. Exam mein sahi shakal hi likhiye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Har identity ki wajah, definition \(y = \log_a x \Leftrightarrow a^{y} = x\) se:
\(\log_a 1 = 0\), kyun ke kisi bhi base ki power zero \(1\) deti hai: \(a^{0} = 1\).
\(\log_a a = 1\), kyun ke \(a^{1} = a\). Yani base ka log usi base mein hamesha 1.
\(\log_a(a^{x}) = x\): pehle power di, phir log liya; log ne power ka kaam ulta kar diya aur \(x\) wapas mil gaya.
\(a^{\log_a x} = x\): pehle log liya, phir power di; power ne log ka kaam ulta kar diya.
Yaani \(a^{x}\) aur \(\log_a x\) ek doosre ko cancel karte hain, kisi bhi tarteeb mein. Bilkul jaise taala lagana aur chaabi se kholna: ek kaam doosre ko ulta kar deta hai. Inverse functions ki yahi pehchaan hai.
Khud sochiye: \(\log_5 25\) kitna hai? Aur \(7^{\log_7 3}\)? (Jawab: 2 aur 3.)
Laws of Logarithms and Change of Base Formula

\(a > 0\), \(a \ne 1\), \(x > 0\), \(y > 0\), \(t \in \mathbb{R}\) ke liye logarithms ke yeh laws aur change of base formula hum pehle parh chuke hain. Inhein dobara dekh lete hain, kyun ke aage graphs aur equations mein inhi se kaam lena hai:

items: Change of Base Formula: \(\log_a x = \frac{\log_b x}{\log_b a}\) for every \(b > 0\), \(b \ne 1\). In particular:

blocks.text_alt: log of x to the base a equals ln x over ln a
log of x to the base a equals log x over log a, with common logarithms

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh laws kahan se aaye? Asal mein yeh exponents ke laws hi hain, sirf doosre libaas mein. Maan lijiye \(x = a^{m}\) aur \(y = a^{n}\), yani \(\log_a x = m\) aur \(\log_a y = n\). Ab \(xy = a^{m} a^{n} = a^{m+n}\), is liye \(\log_a(xy) = m + n = \log_a x + \log_a y\). Yani multiply karne se log jama (add) ho jate hain. Isi tarah \(\frac{x}{y} = a^{m-n}\) se quotient law aur \(x^{t} = a^{tm}\) se power law nikalta hai.
Change of base formula kab aur kyun? Calculator par sirf do log buttons hote hain: \(\log\) (base 10) aur \(\ln\) (base \(e\)). Agar \(\log_2 5\) chahiye to seedha button nahi hai. Yahan change of base kaam aata hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal hamari taraf se hai (kitab ka sawal nahi): \(\log_2 5\) nikaaliye.
Change of base se: \(\log_2 5 = \frac{\ln 5}{\ln 2}\).
Calculator se: \(\ln 5 \approx 1.6094\), \(\ln 2 \approx 0.6931\).
Taqseem karne se: \(\log_2 5 \approx 2.3219\).
Tasdeeq: \(2^{2}= 4\) aur \(2^{3} = 8\), aur 5 in dono ke darmiyan hai, is liye jawab 2 aur 3 ke darmiyan hona chahiye. Bilkul aisa hi hai.
Khud sochiye: \(\log_2 32\) aur \(\log_4 2\) kitne hain? (Jawab: 5 aur \(\frac{1}{2}\), kyun ke \(2^{5} = 32\) aur \(4^{1/2} = 2\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(y = \log_a x\) ka matlab \(a^{y} = x\); shartein: \(a > 0\), \(a \ne 1\), \(x > 0\).
2. \(\log_a x\), \(a^{x}\) ka inverse hai: domain \(]0, \infty[\), range \(]-\infty, \infty[\). Domain aur range aapas mein badal jate hain.
3. \(\log b\) ka matlab \(\log_{10} b\) (common), aur \(\ln b\) ka matlab \(\log_e b\) (natural).
4. \(\log_a 1 = 0\), \(\log_a a = 1\), \(\log_a(a^{x}) = x\), \(a^{\log_a x} = x\).
5. Product, quotient, power laws; change of base \(\log_a x = \frac{\ln x}{\ln a}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\log_a(x + y)\) ko \(\log_a x + \log_a y\) likh dena. Product law \(xy\) ke liye hai, \(x + y\) ke liye nahi. Jama ka log aage nahi tootta.
2. \(\frac{\log_a x}{\log_a y}\) ko \(\log_a \frac{x}{y}\) samajhna. Quotient law yeh hai: \(\log_a \frac{x}{y} = \log_a x - \log_a y\) (minus, divide nahi).
3. Zero ya negative number ka log lena: \(\log_a x\) ke liye \(x > 0\) zaroori hai. \(\log(-5)\) real numbers mein exist nahi karta.
4. Kitab ki chhapai wali ghalat identity \(\log_a x = x\) yaad kar lena. Sahi: \(a^{\log_a x} = x\).
